yt_description:
Shopping for a 2003–05 Range Rover with the 4.4 V8? Listen for a rattle at start-up. The BMW M62 uses plastic timing-chain guides; as the tensioner weakens, the chain slaps them until they break. A full kit (Atlantic British TCKL322) runs about $1,850, and one owner logged about 26 hours doing it with the engine in. Cheap insurance: a new tensioner early can save the guides.

The whole job, step by step: https://boxytrucks.com/repairs/range-rover/l322/bmw-m62-timing-chain-guides/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=hook-test

Photos: Draco2008 · CC BY 2.0 · txomcs. Voiceover is AI-generated.
yt_comment: Thanks for watching! It doesn't happen to every truck: an L322 owners' poll on AULRO came out about 50/50, and some engines pass 200,000 miles with no guide trouble. One owner found his guides intact but very brittle at 235,000 km and suggests doing them around then, or sooner if you hear a rattle. If the guides do break, drop the sump and clear the pieces from the oil pickup. The full job, the parts and the mistakes: https://boxytrucks.com/repairs/range-rover/l322/bmw-m62-timing-chain-guides/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=comment Has yours had the guides done?
